# P21 — realistic bootstrap suite: run evidence and findings

**Date:** 2026-10-12 · **Engine:** `backtest` release binary, `--scenarios-dir tests/scenarios-realistic`
**Suite:** 12 scenarios generated by `tools/scenarios/generate_realistic.py` (seed 20261012)
**Report artifacts:** `docs/backtest-report-realistic.md` / `.json`

This run tests the engine against paths built from the real Perpl testnet tape
instead of hand-authored ones. It produced five findings, one of which is a
design issue in the tier thresholds. All of them are reported as-is.

---

## 1. Input calibration (real tape)

960 one-minute candles pulled live from `https://testnet.perpl.xyz/api` for ETH
(market 32) and BTC (market 16); stored in
`docs/evidence/p21-perpl-real-candles.json`. The captured window contained a
live -3.1% ETH drawdown.

| series | σ/min | annualized vol | skew | excess kurtosis | jumps > 4σ | largest |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ETH 1m | 0.000775 | 56.2% | -0.80 | +10.22 | 6 | 7.6σ |
| BTC 1m | 0.000522 | 37.8% | -0.08 | +3.20 | 5 | 5.5σ |
| SOL 1m | 0.001067 | 77.3% | -0.51 | +8.61 | 10 | 6.7σ |

corr(ETH,BTC) 1m = **+0.759** · acf1(|ETH ret|) = **+0.262** (volatility
clustering) · acf1(ETH ret) = +0.041.

Paths are block bootstraps (30-bar blocks) of that tape; multi-asset scenarios
reuse the same block indices so the real correlation carries through. Regime
injections are calibrated to the observed tails (5.5-7.5σ gap, 7-14% crash over
8-20 bars, and so on). Full method: `tests/scenarios-realistic/README.md`.

aggregate: 12 scenarios, notional $38533.499, saved $394.02 (1.02%),

number (`sim_fees_usd` per scenario).

---

## Finding 1 — the tier bands are absolute, so high leverage trims at open (design issue)

**10 of the 12 scenarios acted on the very first tick** (`bar 0`), before the
tape had moved at all. The cause is arithmetic, not tape:

- The thresholds are `soft 25 / warn 15 / hard 8` percent distance to
  liquidation.
- A position's opening distance is `(1 - 1/leverage) / (1 - maintenance)`:
  3.5% at 12x, 5.3% at 10x, 7.9% at 8x, 15.8% at 5x.
- So **any position opened at roughly 5x or higher starts inside the Orange
  band, and 8x or higher starts inside Red** — with no adverse move.

The engine is behaving exactly as specified; the specification is what deserves
review. Distance-to-liquidation is being read as if it were a market signal,
when at open it is a function of the user's own leverage choice. Two candidate
fixes:

1. Normalize the bands against the position's own entry-to-liquidation span
   (e.g. Red when price has covered 80% of the distance from entry to liq),
   so a fresh position is always Green by construction.
2. Gate the first action on having observed at least one adverse move (a
   `min_move_since_open` criterion), which preserves the absolute bands but
   stops the engine from trading its own entry.

This is a policy/threshold decision, not a code defect, and it changes the
frozen P13 numbers, so it is reported here rather than applied unilaterally.

## Finding 2 — protection has a cost, and this suite prices it

Two scenarios with negative savings, both honest:

- `rb-04-whipsaw-recovery-6x`: **-$3.21** on $2,475 notional (-0.13%). The
  engine trimmed into a drawdown that then fully recovered. That is the real
  cost of insurance when the event does not arrive.
- `rb-07-short-squeeze-10x`: -$0.21, i.e. fees.

Across the suite, cost is small against the avoided tail: the same engine
saved $145.93 on the two-leg portfolio and $133.45 on the correlated crash.
But the negative cases belong in the report, not in a footnote.

## Finding 3 — the false-positive metric is deliberately harsh

The harness defines `false_positive_reduces` as *every executed reduce* in any
scenario whose baseline never liquidated (`engine.rs:636`). The suite counts
**26**. That number should be read as an upper bound: it is the count of
protective reduces that a strictly-outcome-based judge would call unnecessary,
including the ones that were correct at the time. It is the conservative
reading, and it is reported that way.

## Finding 4 — "liquidations avoided" is structural, not measured

`sentinel_liquidations` is hard-coded to `0` (`engine.rs:654`) because the
sentinel side uses the frozen P13 §5 formula-only accounting: realized PnL +
final unrealized PnL + fees. A sentinel position that crosses its liquidation
price is **noted** (`sentinel position crossed its liq price at ... ms
(formula-only accounting, P13 §5)`), never terminated.

Consequence: `liquidations_avoided == baseline_liquidations` by construction.
It cannot fail, so on its own it is not evidence. **The honest metrics are the
dollar deltas** (`baseline_loss_usd` vs `sentinel_loss_usd`), which is what the
tables in this document use.

`rb-10` shows this plainly: the sentinel path logged **9 crossings** in the
notes while still producing a final PnL. On a live venue the exchange's
liquidation engine would very likely have taken the position before any
reactive order could fill.

## Finding 5 — the gap control: a gap is not recoverable, and the numbers say so

`rb-10-gap-through-liq-12x` was designed as the negative control: a -16% gap at
bar 2, far past the -3.5% liquidation of a 12x long. The gap was injected
immediately (bar 1-3) so no pre-gap tape could flatter the engine.

Result: baseline loss **$103.10** (liquidated), sentinel loss **$97.83**. The
$5.27 difference is the head start from the tick-0 trim that Finding 1
describes, not a rescued position. The honest summary: **when price gaps
through liquidation, you lose the position either way; the guardian's value is
in the bars before the gap, not at the gap.**

The same run also validates the two cases where doing nothing is correct:
`rb-05` (4x long, 21% from liquidation) and `rb-09` (3x long, 30% away, on an
undamped real-volatility tape) both produced **zero actions**. The engine can
be quiet.

---

## Reproducing

```bash
python3 tools/scenarios/generate_realistic.py
cargo build --release --bin backtest
./target/release/backtest --scenarios-dir tests/scenarios-realistic --out docs/backtest-report-realistic
```

Seeded and deterministic: the same `--seed` reproduces the suite byte for byte.
The candle input is committed at
`docs/evidence/p21-perpl-real-candles.json` so the run does not need the
network.
